title: latency-regression-detector-and-prime-suite
author: Diego Ramos
release_notes: Adds a lightweight latency regression detector and a deterministic 'prime' workload runner for continuous micro-regression detection; non-breaking. Includes dashboard and alert wiring.
description:
Context and motivation: We occasionally observe subtle latency regresses (microsecond-level shifts) that don't fail existing throughput or end-to-end tests but cause SLA drift on tail latency. This PR introduces a small end-to-end pipeline to (1) generate a deterministic high-fidelity micro-workload (the 'prime' suite), (2) run that workload in CI and on perf-canary, (3) export compact latency histograms, and (4) run a statistical latency-regression-detector that flags sustained shifts and creates a structured report. The goal is fast detection of small regressions and a reliable baseline to compare runtime/kernel changes.

What this PR contains (summary):
- latency/detector: new detector service that consumes histogram exports and computes change points using a simplified CUSUM + bootstrap p-value heuristic.
- tools/prime-runner: deterministic request generator that reproduces a carefully chosen sequence of batch/seqlen mixes (seeded RNG) to surface cache-warmup and KV-cache effects.
- reports/exporter: compact protobuf exporter and an HTTP endpoint used by the detector to fetch benchmark artifacts.
- ci/bench-ci.yml: CI pipeline job that runs a short prime-suite and posts artifacts.
- dashboards/latency-regress.json: Grafana panel + alert rule wiring for the detector output.
- tests: unit and integration tests that run the detector against synthetic shifts and verify alert thresholds.

Commits (high-level):
- Initial detector scaffold and CUSUM+bootstrap implementation.
- Prime-suite runner with deterministic seed and small workload corpus (1k requests) targeting typical LLM client patterns.
- Exporter proto + small local HTTP server for artifacts.
- CI job and GitHub Actions integration for nightly/PR checks.
- Docs and runbook for interpreting detector output and triage steps.
- Fixes from review: lower false-positive rate, add golden traces, tighten timeouts.

Changed files (high level):
- latency/detector/main.go (new)
- latency/detector/cusum.go (new)
- tools/prime-runner/runner.py (new)
- reports/exporter/server.go (new)
- ci/bench-ci.yml (modified)
- dashboards/latency-regress.json (new)
- tests/detector_test.go (new)
- docs/perf/latency-regression-detector.md (new)
- Makefile (modified to add bench target)

Testing and CI: The bench CI job was flaky on the first run due to a 2s timeout on the exporter upload; I extended timeouts and re-ran. Full bench pipeline passed on the second run: standalone prime-suite + detector integration completed in ~90s on the CI runner. Unit tests for CUSUM/bootstrapping passed locally and in CI. Recorded artifacts are attached to the PR run for reproducibility.

Review summary and discussion:
- Priya: requested determinism for the prime-suite and explicit RNG seeds. Addressed in commit 4 (runner.py now accepts a seed and records it in metadata).
- Ava: asked for rationale for using CUSUM vs. EWMA; replied that CUSUM is more sensitive to small sustained shifts and is simpler to reason about; added a short note in docs comparing both approaches and a one-line flag to switch detector mode.
- Samir: requested lowering the alerting sensitivity to avoid noise during rollout; I added a 3-sample confirmation window and a debounce period documented in runbook.
- QA note: added golden traces and a small deterministic regression scenario to avoid flaky detector behavior.

Manual verification steps performed before merge:
1) Run prime-suite locally against a dev-serving instance, confirm reproducible histograms with same seed.
2) Inject a synthetic +8% tail shift into exported histogram and verify detector flags it within 3 runs.
3) Validate dashboard renders detector summary and links to artifacts.

Rollout and operational plan:
- Merged to main and added bench CI job as optional for fast PRs, nightly as required for main branches.
- Perf-oncall will monitor alerts for the first week; runbook owner: Priya Patel.
- If false-positives appear, lowering sensitivity or increasing confirmation window is the first mitigation.

Why this is different from existing benchmark runners: The prime-suite is intentionally small and deterministic (1k request corpus) and focuses on surface cache-warmup, prefix/KV-cache interaction, and batching transitions. The detector is lightweight and designed to be runnable in <2 minutes so it can be included in PR checks and nightly canary runs.

Followups (tracked in linked Linear items):
- ENG-4821: add multi-region comparison and cross-model baselines.
- ENG-4940: tune detector thresholds with long-term corpora and integrate with alerting pager policy.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after reviewers approved. Attachments: CI artifact links, example detector report JSON (artifact id: artifact-20240422-primereport).

If you want to run locally: make bench && ./tools/prime-runner/runner.py --seed 42 --target http://localhost:8080/export
